summary: This article explains why corals turn white when the sea stays too warm, what happens to a bleached coral, and how reefs, fish, and people in places like Saudi Arabia help coral recover.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Coral Bleaching and How Reefs Recover” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: a tiny sea animal with a soft body, such as a single coral
very small plant-like living things that grow in water
the hard frame that supports or protects a body

challengeTerms.def: a hard rock made mostly from the remains of sea animals and shells
describing a close relationship in which two living things help each other
the young form of some animals, which looks very different from the adult

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that coral reefs can be saved if people act now? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a coral reef can recover after bleaching.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review polyp, algae, and skeleton, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use limestone, symbiotic, and larvae in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
